purpose: Phenoxybenzamine is used to manage a rare tumor called a pheochromocytoma, which sits on the adrenal gland and releases hormones that cause dangerously high blood pressure. It helps control blood pressure spikes and sweating caused by this tumor. It is often used before surgery to remove the tumor to make the procedure safer.
how_it_works: Your body has chemical messengers called adrenaline and noradrenaline that can cause blood vessels to tighten and blood pressure to rise. Phenoxybenzamine blocks special receptors called alpha receptors that these messengers normally attach to. By permanently blocking these receptors, the medication keeps blood vessels relaxed and blood pressure under better control.
common_side_effects: Low blood pressure especially when standing up quickly (which can cause dizziness or lightheadedness), fast heartbeat, stuffy nose, dry mouth, tiredness, and difficulty ejaculating in men. You may also feel flushed or warm.
warnings: Be very careful when standing up from sitting or lying down, as your blood pressure can drop suddenly and cause fainting. Avoid activities that require alertness if you feel dizzy. Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, kidney problems, or are pregnant. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first. It can interact with other blood pressure medications, so always share your full medication list with your healthcare team.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 10 mg taken by mouth twice a day. Your doctor will slowly increase your dose every few days, usually up to 20 to 40 mg two or three times daily, depending on how your body responds and your blood pressure readings. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
